ex-adversum (-vors- ) and ex-adversus (-vors- ), adv. and
I.praep. Lit. from opposite; hence, over against, opposite, vis-a\-vis.
I. Adv.: “apud ipsum lacum est pistrilla, et exadversum fabrica,” Ter. Ad. 4, 2, 44 : “video exadvorsum Pistoclerum,” Plaut. Bacch. 4, 7, 37 : “ea sita erat exadvorsum,” Ter. Phorm. 1, 2, 47 : “inque earum locum bina castra exadversum constituta erant,” Suet. Caes. 40 Roth; App. Flor. p. 353; Amm. 23, 6, 72.—With dat.: “exadvorsum ei loco Tonstrina erat quaedam,” Ter. Phorm. 1, 2, 38 : “Samos est exadversum Mileto,” App. Flor. p. 350, 23 ; id. Mag. p. 284, 2.—
II. Praep. with acc.: ara Aio Loquenti exadversus eum locum consecrata est, * Cic. Div. 1, 45, 101: “exadversum Athenas classem suam constituerunt,” Nep. Them. 3 fin. ; id. Thras. 2 fin.; Plin. 6, 16, 18, § 48. Cf. Hand, Turs. II. pp. 662-664.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
